mark_split.label: Write as a quadratic in cosθ

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.107, chapter 9 TRIGONOMETRIC EQUATIONS, Short Answer question 2(i). Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1+1+1 shape gives one mark to each root because BOTH survive here — the surd coefficient makes students expect a rejection, and this question is the one in the set where no root is discarded. EXTRANEOUS-ROOT RECORD: nothing is squared and no denominator is cleared, so no candidate can enter that the original equation refuses. Both cosθ = √3/2 and cosθ = 1/2 lie inside [−1, 1] and both were substituted back: 4(3/4) + √3 = 3 + √3 against 2(√3+1)(√3/2) = 3 + √3, and 4(1/4) + √3 = 1 + √3 against 2(√3+1)(1/2) = √3 + 1. The card says both are kept and why, so a student does not discard one out of habit. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Equations supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Write as a quadratic in cosθ
steps.margin_note: First mark. Only cosθ appears, so no identity is needed. Bring every term to the left and read the equation as a quadratic with cosθ as the unknown.
steps.memory_tip: Only cosine appears, so no identity is needed — just move everything to one side.
lines: This is a quadratic in cosθ.

recall.must_convey: That every term is moved to one side, giving a quadratic in cosθ.
accept: bring everything to the left so it is four cos squared minus two root three plus one cos theta plus root three equals zero
no identity is needed because only cosine appears
read it as a quadratic with cos theta as the unknown
anni oka vaipuki teesukoni cos theta lo quadratic ga chudali
write it in standard quadratic form

steps.why: The equation already holds one ratio, so the Pythagorean identity is not needed. Recognising it as a quadratic is the only insight this step asks for.
common_mistakes: Replacing cos²θ by 1 − sin²θ and creating a second ratio.
Losing the sign when moving 2(√3 + 1) cosθ across.

steps.label: Split the middle term
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expand 2(√3 + 1) as 2√3 + 2 and split the middle term into those two pieces. The bracket (2cosθ − √3) is then shared.
steps.memory_tip: 2(√3 + 1) = 2√3 + 2, and the split is already written for you: −2√3 cosθ and −2cosθ.

recall.must_convey: That the middle term splits as −2√3 cosθ − 2cosθ, giving (2cosθ − √3)(2cosθ − 1) = 0.
accept: expand two into root three plus one and split the middle term into minus two root three cos and minus two cos
the factors are two cos theta minus root three and two cos theta minus one
the coefficient itself tells you how to split it
middle term ni two root three, two ga split cheyyali
factorise into the two brackets
heard_as: two cos theta minus root three

steps.why: The coefficient 2(√3 + 1) is already written as a sum, so the split needs no searching — the two pieces of that sum ARE the two parts of the middle term.
common_mistakes: Using the quadratic formula and mishandling √(16 − 8√3).
Splitting as −√3 cosθ − (√3 + 2) cosθ, which shares no bracket.

steps.label: Solve the first factor
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Both roots lie inside [−1, 1], so neither is discarded — say so, because the surds make students expect a rejection. Then solve cosθ = √3/2.
steps.memory_tip: Check the range before solving: √3/2 ≈ 0.87 and 1/2 are both inside [−1, 1], so BOTH roots are kept.
lines: Both lie between −1 and 1, so both are kept.
Now cosθ = √3/2 = cos(π/6), so α = π/6

recall.must_convey: That both roots are inside [−1, 1] and cosθ = √3/2 gives θ = 2nπ ± π/6.
accept: both roots are inside minus one to one so both are kept and cos theta root three by two gives two n pi plus or minus pi by six
check the range first, neither root is discarded
cos theta is root three over two which is cos pi by six
rendu roots range lo unnayi, edi reject cheyyakoodadu
solve the first bracket with the cosine general solution
heard_as: two n pi plus or minus

steps.why: Checking the range is a habit worth keeping even when nothing fails it — here both values are possible cosines, so discarding one would lose half the answer.
common_mistakes: Discarding cosθ = 1/2 as if it were out of range.
Using the sine general solution nπ + (−1)ⁿα for a cosine equation.

steps.label: Solve the second factor
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cosθ = 1/2 is cos(π/3). Write BOTH families in the final answer, joined by 'or', with n ∈ Z.
steps.memory_tip: cosθ = 1/2 = cos(π/3). Two factors, two families — write both in the final line.
lines: Now cosθ = 1/2 = cos(π/3), so α = π/3
Both families are solutions of the equation.

lines.text: ∴ θ = 2nπ ± π/6 or 2nπ ± π/3, n ∈ Z

recall.must_convey: That cosθ = 1/2 gives θ = 2nπ ± π/3, and BOTH families are written in the answer.
accept: cos theta is a half which is cos pi by three so theta is two n pi plus or minus pi by three
write both families two n pi plus or minus pi by six and two n pi plus or minus pi by three
the second bracket gives pi by three as the principal value
cos theta half ante cos pi by three, rendu families rasali
give both answers with n belongs to Z
heard_as: two n pi plus or minus

steps.why: Each factor of the quadratic is a separate equation with its own family of angles. A final answer that names only one of them answers half the question.
common_mistakes: Writing only one of the two families.
Combining them into a single nπ ± α line, which is a different set.
